title: A published envelope's schemaVersion does not change when the payload shape does, so a consumer has no way to pick a decoder
description:
Reported by host mbpm2 (routed via opum-agent, OPAG-140), observed against a real integration consumer of the published CLIs: their 0.6.2 validation PASSED (99 workflow tests, zero skips) but their own consumer broke afterward anyway. Root cause: QCLI-264 (Done, this repository) unified mutating commands so `data.task` became bare `data` in the {schemaVersion, kind, data, principal} envelope -- a real, deliberate, correctly-shipped shape change -- but both the pre-QCLI-264 shape and the post-QCLI-264 shape report schemaVersion: 1. mbpm2 had no machine-readable field to branch a decoder on; they ask for versioned command-output schemas, or a contract version, and explicitly note the outer envelope's version could stay separate from it.

This is a defect, not a feature request: a version field that doesn't change when the shape changes reports "unchanged" about something that changed. Same class as lore CLI's ManifestFlag, which can't express requiredness at all, so `lore manifest --json` tells an agent a mandatory flag is optional -- and the headline example for 0.7.0's shared cross-repo principle (being settled with lore-cli): anything an agent parses must be able to express what it does not currently say.

CRITICAL INPUT FROM opum-cli-e2e, who read their own suite before this was filed -- the two candidate fixes have opposite blast radii:

1. Bump the schemaVersion VALUE. lib/harness.mjs:19 holds CONTRACT.schemaVersion = 1 as one hardcoded constant, checked by strict equality for every quest row in every suite. A bump turns every quest row red at once -- loud, not silent, but needs a deliberate reviewed change on opum-cli-e2e's side, not a surprise landing under them.
2. Add a separate discriminator field alongside schemaVersion: 1. Their successEnvelope never rejects unknown top-level keys, so this is safe and non-breaking -- and completely unverified, because nothing there reads it today. The fix meant to let a consumer choose a decoder would ship with nothing proving a consumer actually can.

Do not implement before coordinating the shape choice with opum-cli-e2e directly -- they are adding shape-locked reads to cover exactly this, and the choice determines what those reads assert against.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A shape (bump the schemaVersion value, add a separate discriminator field, or another option) is decided jointly with opum-cli-e2e and recorded here with reasoning before implementation starts

A published or CI-pre-publish envelope for a command whose payload shape has changed carries a machine-readable signal distinct from one whose shape hasn't, verified against opum-cli-e2e's shape-locked reads rather than only this repository's own tests
mbpm2's specific defect (data.task -> data with an unchanged schemaVersion) is either retroactively expressible under the new signal or explicitly documented as a pre-signal gap that will not recur
The decision and rationale are recorded somewhere durable a publisher will read (CHANGELOG and/or a decision record), not only in this task's own notes

implementationNotes: Shape settled with opum-cli-e2e (cross-session, both sides agreed): a new top-level contractVersion field, integer, GLOBAL not per-command (their call -- bounded coarse-recheck cost beats an unbounded per-command versioning obligation), starting at 1 in the release that introduces it. Implemented at the single real serialization site, output() in src/cli/main.ts (the ~40 other 'schemaVersion: 1' occurrences in command-contract.ts are either the CommandManifestEntry per-command manifest declarations, a separate/unrelated mechanism, or the untouched task-binding v1 protocol at main.ts:2452, which already carries its own explicit versioning and is out of scope). Also updated the domain ResultEnvelope type and the success() helper (application/command-contract.ts), which is dead at runtime but is the direct subject of the 'frozen Opum wire shape' contract test, so it needed to state the real shape too. bun run check: 482/482 green after fixing the one exact-envelope test it broke (integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts). CHANGELOG.md Unreleased documents the field and states plainly that data.task->data (QCLI-264/265) predates the signal and stays undetectable by it -- not backdated. AC2 (verified against opum-cli-e2e's own locked read) stays open until they confirm against the actual shipped path post-merge; will ping them with it.

THE FINDING. The CHANGELOG entry for contractVersion said what the field covers and never what it does not -- which is the same defect this task exists to fix, applied to this task own fix. A field that cannot express what it does not say is the ManifestFlag shape.

MEASURED, by probing every envelope family the real 0.7.0 binary emits (the qualification artifact, not the source, and not the installed 0.6.2):
- contractVersion: 1 present on every success envelope, no gaps, across task view/list/status-flow, search, board, overview, doctor, manifest, instructions, milestone/draft/decision list and agents --check.
- Both error paths carry NO contractVersion. 0.6.2 error envelope is byte-identical to 0.7.0s, so nothing is broken today -- but "contractVersion absent implies pre-0.7.0 shape" is therefore an invalid rule about error envelopes, and nothing said so.
- The 0.7.0 pause rename (Blocked to Paused) is a configured-value change inside an unchanged payload shape. The counter correctly stays 1 by its own definition while a string-matching consumer breaks. Correct behaviour, surprising reading.

WHY NO CODE CHANGE, and this is the part that settles it rather than deferring it. I read opum-cli-e2e harness directly instead of assuming symmetry with their successEnvelope: lib/check.mjs:181-183, errorEnvelope validates against a strict allow-list of {error_type, message, hint, input, principal} and reports any extra key as a failure. Their successEnvelope tolerates unknown top-level keys -- which is exactly why shipping contractVersion there was safe and non-breaking. So adding contractVersion to error envelopes turns a real consumers checks red WHENEVER it happens, before this tag or after it. The usual "defer it, additive fields are cheap" reasoning does not apply here: deferring to 0.8.0 would not have been cheaper, only later, while leaving 0.7.0 looking like an oversight in the meantime. Documenting the omission as deliberate is the resolution, not a postponement of one.

This strengthens AC4 (already checked): the durable record a publisher reads now states the boundary, not just the capability.

It was the right read of the text and the wrong prediction of the ruling -- the gap was in the Spec, which the amendment closed, not in 0.7.0. Method lesson kept in the repository profile: when a contract is silent, say "undetermined" and route it; do not infer from a neighbouring clause reasoning. Arguing by analogy from the PrincipalRef ratification bar pointed the OPPOSITE way from where this landed.
2. I told lore-cli their target.body finding was "squarely addressed by the spec" and it is NOT. The breaking clause says "an existing ENVELOPE field" and enumerates the four top-level keys; the permitted list separately says "adding fields to data"; removing a field from inside data is on neither list. Verified by grep before conceding. I read "removing an existing field" and stopped before the qualifier that changed its scope.
3. opum-cli-e2e strict error-envelope allow-list (lib/check.mjs:181-183) is now a CONSUMER DEFECT under the amendment, not a constraint either CLI must design around. Our shared "there is no cheap moment to add envelope metadata to an error envelope" conclusion is VOID. They verified independently, agreed, and filed their TASK-66 to fix it after the 0.7.0 baseline is cut. Treat it as a practical blocker only -- red rows block a release whatever the Spec says -- but the fix is theirs.

RULE RECORDED IN THE REPOSITORY PROFILE (both halves, from lore-cli, who raised them):
1. The lockstep is a fact about VERSIONS, not SHAs. Re-verify by reading package.json and the tags, never the tip SHA. A tracker-only or docs-only commit on either side moves a SHA and unpairs nothing; treating that as drift wastes a session. lore-cli has the same rule on LCLI-496.
2. Assert the refs AFTER a promotion push instead of trusting its exit code. Their first promotion failed on intermittent SSH Permission denied (publickey) and main did not move; they only knew because a post-push assertion ran. In a scrollback an auth-failed push and a stale-ref silent no-op (ODOC-193) look identical. Use the GitHub API for the assertion -- token auth, unaffected by the SSH failure that broke the push.

Also recorded: read package.json at the exact SHA rather than at a branch name, because a branch can move between two API calls and a SHA cannot.

THE LORE ASYMMETRY IS SETTLED, AND NOT AS A DEFECT. lore 0.7.0 emits no contractVersion anywhere -- measured by lore-cli against the 0.7.0 tree, not the 0.6.2 on their PATH. So a consumer writing `if ('contractVersion' in envelope)` gets true from quest and false from lore at the same version. ODOC-195 (opum-doc PR #274) ruled on 2026-09-15 before either tag: top-level envelope key sets are OPEN to addition on both envelopes, a consumer MUST tolerate an unrecognised top-level key, ratification applies only to identity-bearing keys, and contractVersion is named conformant explicitly. Both CLIs are therefore correct at 0.7.0. RECORD IT AS A RULING ALREADY MADE, not a known asymmetry to remedy -- filed the same way on lore's side as LCLI-501. Nobody should re-open it.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS TASK'S OWN REASONING, which is worth more than the outcome. QCLI-289 kept contractVersion off the error envelope because opum-cli-e2e's check.errorEnvelope allow-lists a closed key set. Read in their file today, lib/check.mjs:189: the allow-list is a NAMED SET -- {error_type, message, hint, input, principal} -- with hint and input optional, and the same check backs both CLIs. lore's five keys ARE that set; quest's three are a subset. So the constraint was never "quest's error envelope is closed at three". It is that contractVersion is not a MEMBER, and adding it would redden a row identically for either CLI. Same decision, materially different reason, and the wrong version of it would have supported a false conclusion -- that quest was specially constrained where lore was not.

WHAT THE PUBLISH ITSELF EXPOSED, filed as QCLI-299 rather than here: a publish can report success while the release is not installable. @opum-ai/quest-darwin-x64@0.7.0 was STAGED -- npm 12's non-public awaiting-2FA state, which occupies the semver index -- for about twelve minutes while the wrapper was live advertising it. Three composing defects in the publish path, and one unknown left explicitly open rather than guessed.
